o1.biggest_strength: It turns the raw data into sharp, checkable conclusions, such as agencies being 60% of Semrush losses and Lite usage limits causing 32% of all churn, and every move has a hard numeric target.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Lite fix offers only a top-up, with no warning before the limit and no look at the price step to Standard, even though in-house buyers name that step as their top loss reason.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a pre-limit warning and a review of the Lite-to-Standard step to Move 2, and make Move 5's success metric tie directly to the study rather than to overall in-house trial share.

o2.biggest_strength: Clear, readable framing with the right moves: a client report that also covers Advanced churners, a fuller Lite fix with a warning, a top-up and a review of the Standard step, and a well-designed holdout test.
o2.biggest_mistake: It puts an invented 'Data as of November 2026' date on the analysis, and several success metrics are vague, such as 'rises above 11%' and 'beats the holdout', so they could not show whether a move really worked.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the made-up date with the real data periods and give each move a specific numeric target, such as agency trial-to-paid reaching 15%.

reason: Both find the same truths and get the maths right. I'd pay slightly more for Output 1 because its targets are concrete enough to judge success, and it asks me to confirm the dates instead of inventing one.
